Parts#

The following classes allow interaction with a vessel’s individual parts.

See also

The parts guide walks the tree of parts, and explains fuel lines, stage numbers and part modules.

  • Part

  • Module

Parts#

Parts

Instances of this class are used to interact with the parts of a vessel. An instance can be obtained by calling GET /space-center/vessel/(id)/parts.

A Parts object is passed and returned as its identifier, a number. A path that acts on an object takes it as (id).

GET /space-center/parts/(id)/all#

A list of all of the vessels parts.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Parts object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (list<SpaceCenter.Part>)

GET /space-center/parts/(id)/root#

The vessels root part.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Parts object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (SpaceCenter.Part)

Note

See the discussion on Traversing the Tree.

GET /space-center/parts/(id)/controlling#

The part from which the vessel is controlled. Returns null if the vessel has no control point, in which case it is oriented by its root part.

Note

A vessel gets no control point when it is created by a decoupler or an undocking and none of its parts is a command module with crew aboard. A probe core does not give it one either. Assign this property to choose the control point, which is equivalent to “Control From Here” in game.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Parts object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (SpaceCenter.Part?)

PUT /space-center/parts/(id)/controlling#

The part from which the vessel is controlled. Returns null if the vessel has no control point, in which case it is oriented by its root part.

Note

A vessel gets no control point when it is created by a decoupler or an undocking and none of its parts is a command module with crew aboard. A probe core does not give it one either. Assign this property to choose the control point, which is equivalent to “Control From Here” in game.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Parts object.

Request JSON Object:

  • value (SpaceCenter.Part?) – The new value.

POST /space-center/parts/(id)/with-name#

A list of parts whose GET /space-center/part/(id)/name is name.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Parts object.

Request JSON Object:

  • name (string) – The name of the part.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (list<SpaceCenter.Part>)

POST /space-center/parts/(id)/with-title#

A list of all parts whose GET /space-center/part/(id)/title is title.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Parts object.

Request JSON Object:

  • title (string) – The title of the part.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (list<SpaceCenter.Part>)

POST /space-center/parts/(id)/with-tag#

A list of all parts whose GET /space-center/part/(id)/tag is tag.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Parts object.

Request JSON Object:

  • tag (string) – The name tag of the part.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (list<SpaceCenter.Part>)

POST /space-center/parts/(id)/with-module#

A list of all parts that contain a Module whose GET /space-center/module/(id)/name is module_name.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Parts object.

Request JSON Object:

  • module_name (string) – The name of the module.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (list<SpaceCenter.Part>)

POST /space-center/parts/(id)/modules-with-name#

A list of modules (combined across all parts in the vessel) whose GET /space-center/module/(id)/name is module_name.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Parts object.

Request JSON Object:

  • module_name (string) – The name of the module.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (list<SpaceCenter.Module>)

GET /space-center/parts/(id)/antennas#

A list of all antennas in the vessel.

Note

A part with several antennas has an entry for each. If RemoteTech is installed, this will always return an empty list. To interact with RemoteTech antennas, use the RemoteTech service APIs.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Parts object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (list<SpaceCenter.Antenna>)

GET /space-center/parts/(id)/cargo-bays#

A list of all cargo bays in the vessel.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Parts object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (list<SpaceCenter.CargoBay>)

GET /space-center/parts/(id)/control-surfaces#

A list of all control surfaces in the vessel.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Parts object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (list<SpaceCenter.ControlSurface>)

GET /space-center/parts/(id)/decouplers#

A list of all decouplers in the vessel.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Parts object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (list<SpaceCenter.Decoupler>)

GET /space-center/parts/(id)/docking-ports#

A list of all docking ports in the vessel.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Parts object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (list<SpaceCenter.DockingPort>)

GET /space-center/parts/(id)/engines#

A list of all engines in the vessel.

Note

This includes any part that generates thrust. This covers many different types of engine, including liquid fuel rockets, solid rocket boosters, jet engines and RCS thrusters.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Parts object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (list<SpaceCenter.Engine>)

GET /space-center/parts/(id)/experiments#

A list of all science experiments in the vessel.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Parts object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (list<SpaceCenter.Experiment>)

GET /space-center/parts/(id)/fairings#

A list of all fairings in the vessel.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Parts object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (list<SpaceCenter.Fairing>)

GET /space-center/parts/(id)/intakes#

A list of all intakes in the vessel.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Parts object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (list<SpaceCenter.Intake>)

GET /space-center/parts/(id)/legs#

A list of all landing legs attached to the vessel.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Parts object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (list<SpaceCenter.Leg>)

GET /space-center/parts/(id)/launch-clamps#

A list of all launch clamps attached to the vessel.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Parts object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (list<SpaceCenter.LaunchClamp>)

GET /space-center/parts/(id)/lights#

A list of all lights in the vessel.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Parts object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (list<SpaceCenter.Light>)

GET /space-center/parts/(id)/parachutes#

A list of all parachutes in the vessel.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Parts object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (list<SpaceCenter.Parachute>)

GET /space-center/parts/(id)/radiators#

A list of all radiators in the vessel.

Part#

Part

Represents an individual part. Vessels are made up of multiple parts. Instances of this class can be obtained by several methods in Parts.

A Part object is passed and returned as its identifier, a number. A path that acts on an object takes it as (id).

GET /space-center/part/(id)/name#

Internal name of the part, as used in part cfg files. For example “Mark1-2Pod”.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (string)

GET /space-center/part/(id)/title#

Title of the part, as shown when the part is right clicked in-game. For example “Mk1-2 Command Pod”.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (string)

GET /space-center/part/(id)/config#

The static configuration of the part, as found in its part cfg file. This provides access to data that is not exposed elsewhere, such as the configuration of the part’s modules. Returns null if the part has no associated configuration node.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (SpaceCenter.ConfigNode)

GET /space-center/part/(id)/tag#

The name tag for the part. Can be set to a custom string using the in-game user interface. Throws an exception if no name tag part module is installed.

Note

Requires KSPCommunityPartModules 0.5 or later, or kOS, which share one name tag.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (string)

PUT /space-center/part/(id)/tag#

The name tag for the part. Can be set to a custom string using the in-game user interface. Throws an exception if no name tag part module is installed.

Note

Requires KSPCommunityPartModules 0.5 or later, or kOS, which share one name tag.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Request JSON Object:

  • value (string) – The new value.

The asset URL for the part’s flag.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (string)

The asset URL for the part’s flag.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Request JSON Object:

  • value (string) – The new value.

Whether the part is highlighted.

Note

The highlighting is removed when the client that enabled it disconnects.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (bool)

PUT /space-center/part/(id)/highlighted#

Whether the part is highlighted.

Note

The highlighting is removed when the client that enabled it disconnects.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Request JSON Object:

  • value (bool) – The new value.

The color used to highlight the part.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (StdLib.ColorRGB)

PUT /space-center/part/(id)/highlight-color#

The color used to highlight the part.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Request JSON Object:

  • value (StdLib.ColorRGB) – The new value.

Response JSON Object:

Response JSON Object:

GET /space-center/part/(id)/parent#

The parts parent. Returns null if the part does not have a parent. This, in combination with GET /space-center/part/(id)/children, can be used to traverse the vessels parts tree.

Parameters:

Response JSON Object:

  • value (SpaceCenter.Part?)

Note

See the discussion on Traversing the Tree.

GET /space-center/part/(id)/children#

The parts children. Returns an empty list if the part has no children. This, in combination with GET /space-center/part/(id)/parent, can be used to traverse the vessels parts tree.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (list<SpaceCenter.Part>)

Note

See the discussion on Traversing the Tree.

Whether the part is axially attached to its parent, i.e. on the top or bottom of its parent. If the part has no parent, returns false.

Response JSON Object:

See the discussion on Attachment Modes.

Note

See the discussion on Attachment Modes.

Note

See the discussion on Staging.

Response JSON Object:

The dynamic pressure acting on the part, in Pascals.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

GET /space-center/part/(id)/static-pressure#

The static pressure acting on the part, in Pascals. Below the waterline this includes the pressure of the water.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

GET /space-center/part/(id)/displacement#

The volume of water the part displaces when fully submerged, in \(\mathrm{m^{3}}\).

Note

See GET /space-center/part/(id)/displaced-volume for the volume it is displacing now.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (double)

GET /space-center/part/(id)/buoyancy-multiplier#

The multiplier applied to the buoyant force on the part. One for most parts.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (float)

POST /space-center/part/(id)/buoyant-force-at#

The buoyant force on the part when fully submerged in a fluid of the given density, in Newtons.

Note

Applies GET /space-center/buoyancy-scalar and GET /space-center/part/(id)/buoyancy-multiplier, so the result is what the game would do to the part rather than what Archimedes’ principle alone gives.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Request JSON Object:

  • density (double) – The density of the fluid, in \(\mathrm{kg/m^{3}}\).

  • gravity (double) – The acceleration due to gravity, in \(\mathrm{m/s^{2}}\).

Response JSON Object:

  • value (double)

GET /space-center/part/(id)/splashed#

Whether the part is in contact with water.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (bool)

GET /space-center/part/(id)/submerged-portion#

The fraction of the part below the waterline, between 0 and 1.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (double)

GET /space-center/part/(id)/displaced-volume#

The volume of water the part is displacing, in \(\mathrm{m^{3}}\).

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (double)

GET /space-center/part/(id)/depth#

The depth of the part below the waterline, in meters, measured at POST /space-center/part/(id)/center-of-displacement. Negative above the waterline. Returns zero if the body the vessel is at has no ocean.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (double)

GET /space-center/part/(id)/min-depth#

The depth of the shallowest point of the part below the waterline, in meters. Returns zero if the body the vessel is at has no ocean.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (double)

GET /space-center/part/(id)/max-depth#

The depth of the deepest point of the part below the waterline, in meters. Returns zero if the body the vessel is at has no ocean.

Note

The game ramps the buoyant force in over the first fraction of a meter of this depth.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (double)

GET /space-center/part/(id)/submerged-dynamic-pressure#

The dynamic pressure of the water acting on the part, in Pascals.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (float)

GET /space-center/part/(id)/submerged-drag-multiplier#

The multiplier applied to the drag on the part while it is submerged.

Note

The game sets this high on splashdown and eases it down as the part moves through the water. It climbs back once the part slows to a crawl, so a hull under way reads lower than one lying still.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (double)

GET /space-center/part/(id)/submerged-lift-multiplier#

The multiplier applied to the lift on the part while it is submerged.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (double)

GET /space-center/part/(id)/water-angular-drag-multiplier#

The multiplier applied to the angular drag on the part while it is submerged.

Note

Part of the part’s configuration rather than a live readout, so it reads the same in the editor and at a body with no ocean.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (float)

GET /space-center/part/(id)/impact-tolerance#

The crash tolerance of the part, in \(\mathrm{m/s}\).

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (double)

GET /space-center/part/(id)/breaking-force#

The breaking force of the part’s attachments, in \(\mathrm{kN}\).

Note

The joint to the parent part takes the lower breaking force of the two parts, scaled by the size of the attachment node. See GET /space-center/part/(id)/joint-break-force.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (float)

GET /space-center/part/(id)/breaking-torque#

The breaking torque of the part’s attachments, in \(\mathrm{kN \cdot m}\).

Note

The joint to the parent part takes the lower breaking torque of the two parts, scaled by the size of the attachment node. See GET /space-center/part/(id)/joint-break-torque.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (float)

GET /space-center/part/(id)/joint-break-force#

The force that breaks the joint to the parent part, in \(\mathrm{kN}\). Throws an exception if the part has no joint to its parent part.

Note

The sum over the joint’s physics joints. It is infinite for a short time after the vessel loads, such as just after launch. The root part and a physicsless part have no joint to their parent.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (float)

GET /space-center/part/(id)/joint-break-torque#

The torque that breaks the joint to the parent part, in \(\mathrm{kN \cdot m}\). Throws an exception if the part has no joint to its parent part.

Note

The sum over the joint’s physics joints. It is infinite for a short time after the vessel loads. On a stack node of size 2 or more, the physics joints sit apart around the node. A bending moment then breaks the joint when one physics joint’s force exceeds its share of GET /space-center/part/(id)/joint-break-force, usually at a much larger moment than this torque.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (float)

GET /space-center/part/(id)/joint-spring#

The spring constant of the joint to the parent part against translation, in \(\mathrm{kN/m}\). Throws an exception if the part has no joint to its parent part.

Note

The sum over the joint’s physics joints. A rigid attachment locks the joint, and this spring then has no effect.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (float)

GET /space-center/part/(id)/joint-damper#

The damping constant of the joint to the parent part against translation, in \(\mathrm{kN \cdot s/m}\). Throws an exception if the part has no joint to its parent part.

Note

The sum over the joint’s physics joints. The stock game sets it to zero, and mods such as Kerbal Joint Reinforcement change it.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (float)

GET /space-center/part/(id)/joint-angular-spring#

The spring constant of the joint to the parent part against bending, in \(\mathrm{kN \cdot m/rad}\). Throws an exception if the part has no joint to its parent part.

Note

The sum over the joint’s physics joints, about the two axes perpendicular to the joint axis. The joint is far stiffer against twisting about its axis. On a stack node of size 2 or more, the physics joints sit apart around the node, and the joint bends much less than this spring gives. A rigid attachment makes it infinite.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (float)

GET /space-center/part/(id)/joint-angular-damper#

The damping constant of the joint to the parent part against bending, in \(\mathrm{kN \cdot m \cdot s/rad}\). Throws an exception if the part has no joint to its parent part.

Note

The sum over the joint’s physics joints. The stock game sets it to zero, and mods such as Kerbal Joint Reinforcement change it.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (float)

A measure of how much energy it takes to increase the internal temperature of the part, in Joules per Kelvin.

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (float)

GET /space-center/part/(id)/thermal-skin-mass#

A measure of how much energy it takes to increase the skin temperature of the part, in Joules per Kelvin.

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (float)

GET /space-center/part/(id)/thermal-resource-mass#

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (float)

GET /space-center/part/(id)/thermal-conduction-flux#

The rate at which heat energy is conducting into or out of the part via contact with other parts. Measured in energy per unit time, or power, in Watts. A positive value means the part is gaining heat energy, and negative means it is losing heat energy.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (float)

GET /space-center/part/(id)/thermal-convection-flux#

The rate at which heat energy is convecting into or out of the part from the surrounding atmosphere. Measured in energy per unit time, or power, in Watts. A positive value means the part is gaining heat energy, and negative means it is losing heat energy.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (float)

GET /space-center/part/(id)/thermal-radiation-flux#

The rate at which heat energy is radiating into or out of the part from the surrounding environment. Measured in energy per unit time, or power, in Watts. A positive value means the part is gaining heat energy, and negative means it is losing heat energy.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (float)

GET /space-center/part/(id)/thermal-internal-flux#

The rate at which heat energy is begin generated by the part. For example, some engines generate heat by combusting fuel. Measured in energy per unit time, or power, in Watts. A positive value means the part is gaining heat energy, and negative means it is losing heat energy.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (float)

GET /space-center/part/(id)/thermal-skin-to-internal-flux#

The rate at which heat energy is transferring between the part’s skin and its internals. Measured in energy per unit time, or power, in Watts. A positive value means the part’s internals are gaining heat energy, and negative means its skin is gaining heat energy.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (float)

POST /space-center/part/(id)/position#

The position of the part in the given reference frame.

Note

This is a fixed position in the part, defined by the parts model. It s not necessarily the same as the parts center of mass. Use POST /space-center/part/(id)/center-of-mass to get the parts center of mass.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Request JSON Object:

  • reference_frame (SpaceCenter.ReferenceFrame) – The reference frame that the returned position vector is in.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (tuple<double, double, double>) – The position as a vector.

POST /space-center/part/(id)/center-of-mass#

The position of the parts center of mass in the given reference frame. If the part is physicsless in flight, this is equivalent to POST /space-center/part/(id)/position.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Request JSON Object:

  • reference_frame (SpaceCenter.ReferenceFrame) – The reference frame that the returned position vector is in.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (tuple<double, double, double>) – The position as a vector.

POST /space-center/part/(id)/bounding-box#

The axis-aligned bounding box of the part in the given reference frame.

Note

This is computed from the meshes that make up the parts model, and covers only this part - the models of any child parts are excluded. If the part has no visible model, the box has zero volume and is centered on the POST /space-center/part/(id)/center-of-mass of the part.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Request JSON Object:

  • reference_frame (SpaceCenter.ReferenceFrame) – The reference frame that the returned position vectors are in.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (SpaceCenter.BoundingBox) – The positions of the minimum and maximum vertices of the box.

POST /space-center/part/(id)/direction#

The direction the part points in, in the given reference frame.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Request JSON Object:

  • reference_frame (SpaceCenter.ReferenceFrame) – The reference frame that the returned direction is in.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (tuple<double, double, double>) – The direction as a unit vector.

POST /space-center/part/(id)/velocity#

The linear velocity of the part in the given reference frame.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Request JSON Object:

  • reference_frame (SpaceCenter.ReferenceFrame) – The reference frame that the returned velocity vector is in.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (tuple<double, double, double>) – The velocity as a vector. The vector points in the direction of travel, and its magnitude is the speed of the body in \(\mathrm{m/s}\).

POST /space-center/part/(id)/rotation#

The rotation of the part, in the given reference frame.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Request JSON Object:

  • reference_frame (SpaceCenter.ReferenceFrame) – The reference frame that the returned rotation is in.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (tuple<double, double, double, double>) – The rotation as a quaternion of the form (x, y, z, w).

POST /space-center/part/(id)/lift#

The aerodynamic lift currently acting on the part.

Note

Not available when Ferram Aerospace Research is installed.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Request JSON Object:

  • reference_frame (SpaceCenter.ReferenceFrame) – The reference frame that the returned vector is in.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (tuple<double, double, double>) – A vector pointing in the direction that the force acts, with its magnitude equal to the strength of the force in Newtons.

Note

Not available when Ferram Aerospace Research is installed.

Request JSON Object:

Response JSON Object:

  • value (tuple<double, double, double>) – A vector pointing in the direction that the force acts, with its magnitude equal to the strength of the force in Newtons.

POST /space-center/part/(id)/center-of-buoyancy#

The point the buoyant force on the part acts at, in the given reference frame.

Note

A submerged part reports the point the game applied the force at, which it shifts towards the submerged part of the hull. Any other part reports its configured center of buoyancy.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Request JSON Object:

  • reference_frame (SpaceCenter.ReferenceFrame) – The reference frame that the returned position vector is in.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (tuple<double, double, double>) – The position as a vector.

POST /space-center/part/(id)/center-of-displacement#

The point the depth of the part is measured at, in the given reference frame.

Parameters:

Request JSON Object:

Response JSON Object:

  • value (tuple<double, double, double>) – The position as a vector.

POST /space-center/part/(id)/buoyant-force#

The buoyant force currently acting on the part.

Note

The buoyant force on its own. The water drag and lift the game applies alongside it are reported by GET /space-center/part/(id)/submerged-drag-multiplier and GET /space-center/part/(id)/submerged-lift-multiplier.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Request JSON Object:

  • reference_frame (SpaceCenter.ReferenceFrame) – The reference frame that the returned vector is in.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (tuple<double, double, double>) – A vector pointing in the direction that the force acts, with its magnitude equal to the strength of the force in Newtons.

The moment of inertia of the part in \(\mathrm{kg \cdot m^{2}}\) around its center of mass in the parts center of mass reference frame (GET /space-center/part/(id)/center-of-mass-reference-frame).

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (tuple<double, double, double>)

GET /space-center/part/(id)/inertia-tensor#

The inertia tensor of the part around its center of mass, in the parts center of mass reference frame (GET /space-center/part/(id)/center-of-mass-reference-frame). Returns the 3x3 matrix as a list of elements, in row-major order.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (list<double>)

GET /space-center/part/(id)/reference-frame#

The reference frame that is fixed relative to this part, and centered on a fixed position within the part, defined by the parts model.

  • The origin is at the position of the part, as returned by POST /space-center/part/(id)/position.

  • The axes rotate with the part.

  • The x, y and z axis directions depend on the design of the part.

Note

For docking port parts, this reference frame is not necessarily equivalent to the reference frame for the docking port, returned by GET /space-center/docking-port/(id)/reference-frame.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (SpaceCenter.ReferenceFrame)

GET /space-center/part/(id)/center-of-mass-reference-frame#

The reference frame that is fixed relative to this part, and centered on its center of mass.

  • The origin is at the center of mass of the part, as returned by POST /space-center/part/(id)/center-of-mass.

  • The axes rotate with the part.

  • The x, y and z axis directions depend on the design of the part.

Note

For docking port parts, this reference frame is not necessarily equivalent to the reference frame for the docking port, returned by GET /space-center/docking-port/(id)/reference-frame.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (SpaceCenter.ReferenceFrame)

POST /space-center/part/(id)/add-force#

Warning

Deprecated. Use Debug.AddForce instead.

Exert a constant force on the part, acting at the given position.

Note

The force is removed when the client that added it disconnects.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Request JSON Object:

  • force (tuple<double, double, double>) – A vector pointing in the direction that the force acts, with its magnitude equal to the strength of the force in Newtons.

  • position (tuple<double, double, double>) – The position at which the force acts, as a vector.

  • reference_frame (SpaceCenter.ReferenceFrame) – The reference frame that the force and position are in.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (SpaceCenter.Force) – An object that can be used to remove or modify the force.

POST /space-center/part/(id)/instantaneous-force#

Warning

Deprecated. Use Debug.InstantaneousForce instead.

Exert an instantaneous force on the part, acting at the given position.

Note

The force is applied instantaneously in a single physics update.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Request JSON Object:

  • force (tuple<double, double, double>) – A vector pointing in the direction that the force acts, with its magnitude equal to the strength of the force in Newtons.

  • position (tuple<double, double, double>) – The position at which the force acts, as a vector.

  • reference_frame (SpaceCenter.ReferenceFrame) – The reference frame that the force and position are in.

GET /space-center/part/(id)/highly-pressurized#

Whether the tank is highly pressurized, which is what a pressure-fed engine needs to draw from (see GET /space-center/engine/(id)/pressure-fed). Throws an exception if the part is not a RealFuels fuel tank (see GET /space-center/part/(id)/has-real-fuels-tank).

Note

Requires RealFuels.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (bool)

GET /space-center/part/(id)/boiloff-rate#

The rate at which the tank’s cryogenic contents are boiling off, in kilograms per second of in-game time, measured over the last update RealFuels computed it in. The contents keep boiling off under time warp, where that update covers a much longer span of in-game time than a physics frame does. The rate is zero for a tank holding nothing cryogenic, for one still being fed by a launch clamp, whose temperature RealFuels holds down instead, and in the editor. Throws an exception if the part is not a RealFuels fuel tank (see GET /space-center/part/(id)/has-real-fuels-tank).

Note

Requires RealFuels.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Part object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (double)

Module#

Module

This can be used to interact with a specific part module. This includes part modules in stock KSP, and those added by mods.

In KSP, each part has zero or more PartModules associated with it. Each one contains some of the functionality of the part. For example, an engine has a “ModuleEngines” part module that contains all the functionality of an engine.

A Module object is passed and returned as its identifier, a number. A path that acts on an object takes it as (id).

GET /space-center/module/(id)/name#

Name of the PartModule. For example, “ModuleEngines”.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Module object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (string)

GET /space-center/module/(id)/part#

The part that contains this module.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Module object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (SpaceCenter.Part)

GET /space-center/module/(id)/config#

The static configuration of the module, as found in the part’s cfg file. This provides access to data that is not exposed as a field, such as the resources produced by a generator. Returns null if the module’s configuration node cannot be found.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Module object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (SpaceCenter.ConfigNode)

Response JSON Object:

A list of all the events of the module, including those not currently visible or active. Events are the clickable buttons visible in the right-click menu of the part. Filter by GET /space-center/part-event/(id)/visible and GET /space-center/part-event/(id)/active to get just the ones shown in the menu.

FieldType

The type of a part module field. See GET /space-center/part-field/(id)/type.

Passed and returned as the name of one of its values:

"boolean"

A boolean field. Access using GET /space-center/part-field/(id)/bool-value.

"integer"

An integer field. Access using GET /space-center/part-field/(id)/int-value.

"float"

A single precision floating point field. Access using GET /space-center/part-field/(id)/float-value.

"double"

A double precision floating point field. Access using GET /space-center/part-field/(id)/double-value.

"string"

A string field. Access using GET /space-center/part-field/(id)/value.

"unknown"

A field whose type is not one of the above. Its value can still be read as a string using GET /space-center/part-field/(id)/value.

  • id – The identifier of the PartEvent object.

PartAction

An action of a part module. These are the part actions that can be assigned to action groups in the in-game editor. Obtained by calling GET /space-center/module/(id)/action-list.

A PartAction object is passed and returned as its identifier, a number. A path that acts on an object takes it as (id).

GET /space-center/part-action/(id)/module#

The part module that contains this action.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the PartAction object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (SpaceCenter.Module)

GET /space-center/part-action/(id)/name#

The identifier of the action. This is stable and does not change between game versions, unlike GET /space-center/part-action/(id)/gui-name.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the PartAction object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (string)

GET /space-center/part-action/(id)/gui-name#

The name of the action, as displayed in the in-game editor.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the PartAction object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (string)

PUT /space-center/part-action/(id)/activated#

Activate or deactivate the action. Equivalent to triggering the action from an action group. Set to true to activate the action, or false to deactivate it.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the PartAction object.

Request JSON Object:

  • value (bool) – The new value.

Config Node#

ConfigNode

Represents a configuration node, as found in a part’s configuration file. A node has a name, a set of named values and a set of child nodes. This is used to access the static configuration of a part or part module, for example via GET /space-center/part/(id)/config and GET /space-center/module/(id)/config.

A ConfigNode object is passed and returned as its identifier, a number. A path that acts on an object takes it as (id).

GET /space-center/config-node/(id)/name#

The name of the configuration node. For example “MODULE”.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the ConfigNode object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (string)

GET /space-center/config-node/(id)/values#

The values stored in the node, as a dictionary mapping names to values.

Note

If a name appears more than once, only the first value is included. Use POST /space-center/config-node/(id)/find-values to get all of the values with a given name.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the ConfigNode object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (dictionary<string, string>)

POST /space-center/config-node/(id)/has-value#

Returns true if the node has a value with the given name.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the ConfigNode object.

Request JSON Object:

  • name (string) – Name of the value.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (bool)

POST /space-center/config-node/(id)/get-value#

Returns the value with the given name. If there is more than one value with the given name, the first is returned. Throws an exception if there is no value with the given name.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the ConfigNode object.

Request JSON Object:

  • name (string) – Name of the value.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (string)

POST /space-center/config-node/(id)/find-values#

Returns all of the values with the given name, as a list.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the ConfigNode object.

Request JSON Object:

  • name (string) – Name of the values.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (list<string>)

GET /space-center/config-node/(id)/nodes#

The child nodes contained in this node.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the ConfigNode object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (list<SpaceCenter.ConfigNode>)

POST /space-center/config-node/(id)/has-node#

Returns true if the node has a child node with the given name.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the ConfigNode object.

Request JSON Object:

  • name (string) – Name of the child node.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (bool)

POST /space-center/config-node/(id)/get-node#

Returns the child node with the given name. If there is more than one child node with the given name, the first is returned. Throws an exception if there is no child node with the given name.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the ConfigNode object.

Request JSON Object:

  • name (string) – Name of the child node.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (SpaceCenter.ConfigNode)

POST /space-center/config-node/(id)/find-nodes#

Returns all of the child nodes with the given name, as a list.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the ConfigNode object.

Request JSON Object:

  • name (string) – Name of the child nodes.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (list<SpaceCenter.ConfigNode>)

Antenna#

Note

If RemoteTech is installed, use the RemoteTech service APIs to interact with antennas. This class covers stock and RealAntennas antennas.

Antenna

An antenna. Obtained by calling GET /space-center/part/(id)/antenna.

A Antenna object is passed and returned as its identifier, a number. A path that acts on an object takes it as (id).

GET /space-center/antenna/(id)/part#

The part object for this antenna.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Antenna object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (SpaceCenter.Part)

GET /space-center/antenna/(id)/state#

The current state of the antenna.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Antenna object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (SpaceCenter.DeployableState)

GET /space-center/antenna/(id)/deployable#

Whether the antenna is deployable.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Antenna object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (bool)

GET /space-center/antenna/(id)/deployed#

Whether the antenna is deployed.

Note

Fixed antennas are always deployed. Throws KRPC.InvalidOperationException if set on a fixed antenna.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Antenna object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (bool)

PUT /space-center/antenna/(id)/deployed#

Whether the antenna is deployed.

Note

Fixed antennas are always deployed. Throws KRPC.InvalidOperationException if set on a fixed antenna.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Antenna object.

Request JSON Object:

  • value (bool) – The new value.

GET /space-center/antenna/(id)/can-transmit#

Whether data can be transmitted by this antenna.

Parameters:

Response JSON Object:

Transmit data.

Parameters:

POST /space-center/antenna/(id)/cancel#

Cancel current transmission of data.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Antenna object.

GET /space-center/antenna/(id)/allow-partial#

Whether partial data transmission is permitted.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Antenna object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (bool)

PUT /space-center/antenna/(id)/allow-partial#

Whether partial data transmission is permitted.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Antenna object.

Request JSON Object:

  • value (bool) – The new value.

GET /space-center/antenna/(id)/power#

The power of the antenna.

Note

Response JSON Object:

GET /space-center/antenna/(id)/combinable#

Response JSON Object:

GET /space-center/antenna/(id)/combinable-exponent#

Exponent used to calculate the combined power of multiple antennae on a vessel.

Note

Not used by RealAntennas, which replaces the stock range model.

Parameters:

Response JSON Object:

  • value (double)

GET /space-center/antenna/(id)/packet-interval#

Interval between sending packets in seconds.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Antenna object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (float)

GET /space-center/antenna/(id)/packet-size#

Amount of data sent per packet in Mits.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Antenna object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (float)

GET /space-center/antenna/(id)/packet-resource-cost#

Units of electric charge consumed per packet sent.

GET /space-center/antenna/(id)/gain#

The gain of the antenna, in \(\mathrm{dBi}\).

Returns the transmit power of the antenna, in \(\mathrm{dBm}\), and sets it in the editor. Throws an exception if set in flight, or outside zero to GET /space-center/antenna/(id)/max-transmit-power.

Note

Requires RealAntennas.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Antenna object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (float)

PUT /space-center/antenna/(id)/transmit-power#

Returns the transmit power of the antenna, in \(\mathrm{dBm}\), and sets it in the editor. Throws an exception if set in flight, or outside zero to GET /space-center/antenna/(id)/max-transmit-power.

Note

Requires RealAntennas.

PUT /space-center/antenna/(id)/tech-level#

Requires RealAntennas.

Note

Requires RealAntennas.

  • id – The identifier of the Antenna object.

Response JSON Object:

GET /space-center/antenna/(id)/band#

The name of the radio frequency band the antenna uses, e.g. "S".

Requires RealAntennas.

Response JSON Object:

The frequency of the antenna’s band, in Hz.

Note

Requires RealAntennas.

Parameters:

Response JSON Object:

GET /space-center/antenna/(id)/data-rate#

The highest data rate the antenna supports, in bits per second.

Note

Requires RealAntennas.

Parameters:

Response JSON Object:

  • value (double)

GET /space-center/antenna/(id)/beamwidth#

The half-power beamwidth of the antenna, in degrees.

Note

Requires RealAntennas.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Antenna object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (double)

GET /space-center/antenna/(id)/idle-power-draw#

The power the antenna draws while idle, in watts.

Note

Requires RealAntennas.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Antenna object.

Response JSON Object:

GET /space-center/antenna/(id)/active-power-draw#

The power the antenna draws while transmitting, in watts. This includes GET /space-center/antenna/(id)/idle-power-draw.

Requires RealAntennas.

Response JSON Object:

GET /space-center/antenna/(id)/enabled#

Returns whether the antenna is enabled, and sets it in the editor. Throws an exception if set in flight.

Note

Requires RealAntennas. A disabled antenna does not communicate and draws no power.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Antenna object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (bool)

PUT /space-center/antenna/(id)/enabled#

Returns whether the antenna is enabled, and sets it in the editor. Throws an exception if set in flight.

Note

Requires RealAntennas. A disabled antenna does not communicate and draws no power.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Antenna object.

Request JSON Object:

  • value (bool) – The new value.

POST /space-center/antenna/(id)/disable-permanently#

Disable the antenna for the rest of the flight. It then draws no power.

Note

Requires RealAntennas.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Antenna object.

GET /space-center/antenna/(id)/can-target#

Whether the antenna can be pointed at a target. Omnidirectional antennas cannot.

Note

Requires RealAntennas.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Antenna object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (bool)

GET /space-center/antenna/(id)/target-mode#

The kind of target the antenna points at.

Note

Requires RealAntennas.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Antenna object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (SpaceCenter.AntennaTargetMode)

GET /space-center/antenna/(id)/target-vessel#

Returns the vessel the antenna points at, and sets the vessel to point at.

Note

Requires RealAntennas. null if the antenna does not point at a vessel. Throws an exception if set to null, or if the antenna cannot be pointed (see GET /space-center/antenna/(id)/can-target).

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Antenna object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (SpaceCenter.Vessel?)

PUT /space-center/antenna/(id)/target-vessel#

Returns the vessel the antenna points at, and sets the vessel to point at.

Note

Requires RealAntennas. null if the antenna does not point at a vessel. Throws an exception if set to null, or if the antenna cannot be pointed (see GET /space-center/antenna/(id)/can-target).

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Antenna object.

Request JSON Object:

  • value (SpaceCenter.Vessel?) – The new value.

GET /space-center/antenna/(id)/target-body#

Returns the body the antenna points at, and sets the body to point at the center of.

Note

Requires RealAntennas. Also the body of a position the antenna points at, or null if it points at neither. Throws an exception if set to null, or if the antenna cannot be pointed (see GET /space-center/antenna/(id)/can-target).

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Antenna object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (SpaceCenter.CelestialBody?)

PUT /space-center/antenna/(id)/target-body#

Returns the body the antenna points at, and sets the body to point at the center of.

Note

Requires RealAntennas. Also the body of a position the antenna points at, or null if it points at neither. Throws an exception if set to null, or if the antenna cannot be pointed (see GET /space-center/antenna/(id)/can-target).

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Antenna object.

Request JSON Object:

  • value (SpaceCenter.CelestialBody?) – The new value.

POST /space-center/antenna/(id)/target-direction#

The direction the antenna points in, in the given reference frame. Throws an exception if the antenna has no target (see GET /space-center/antenna/(id)/target-mode).

Note

Requires RealAntennas.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Antenna object.

Request JSON Object:

  • reference_frame (SpaceCenter.ReferenceFrame) – The reference frame that the returned direction is in.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (tuple<double, double, double>) – The direction as a unit vector.

POST /space-center/antenna/(id)/set-target-position#

Point the antenna at a position on or above a body.

Note

Requires RealAntennas. Throws an exception if the antenna cannot be pointed (see GET /space-center/antenna/(id)/can-target).

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Antenna object.

Request JSON Object:

  • body (SpaceCenter.CelestialBody) – The body.

  • latitude (double) – The latitude, in degrees.

  • longitude (double) – The longitude, in degrees.

  • altitude (double) – The altitude above sea level, in meters.

POST /space-center/antenna/(id)/set-target-azimuth-elevation#

Point the antenna in a direction relative to the vessel’s position on the surface.

Note

Requires RealAntennas. Throws an exception if the antenna cannot be pointed (see GET /space-center/antenna/(id)/can-target).

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Antenna object.

Request JSON Object:

  • azimuth (double) – The azimuth, in degrees clockwise from north, from 0 to 360.

  • elevation (double) – The elevation above the horizon, in degrees, from -90 to 90.

POST /space-center/antenna/(id)/set-target-orbit-relative#

Point the antenna in a direction relative to the vessel’s orbital velocity.

Note

Requires RealAntennas. Throws an exception if the antenna cannot be pointed (see GET /space-center/antenna/(id)/can-target).

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Antenna object.

Request JSON Object:

  • deflection (double) – The angle from the orbital velocity in the orbital plane, in degrees, from -180 to 180.

  • elevation (double) – The angle out of the orbital plane, in degrees, from -90 to 90.

AntennaTargetMode

The kind of target a RealAntennas antenna points at. See GET /space-center/antenna/(id)/target-mode.

Passed and returned as the name of one of its values:

"none"

The antenna has no target. Omnidirectional antennas have none.

"vessel"

A vessel. See GET /space-center/antenna/(id)/target-vessel.

"body"

The center of a body. See GET /space-center/antenna/(id)/target-body.

"position"

A position on or above a body. See POST /space-center/antenna/(id)/set-target-position.

"azimuth_elevation"

An azimuth and elevation from the vessel’s position. See POST /space-center/antenna/(id)/set-target-azimuth-elevation.

"orbit_relative"

A direction relative to the vessel’s orbital velocity. See POST /space-center/antenna/(id)/set-target-orbit-relative.

Cargo Bay#

CargoBay

A cargo bay. Obtained by calling GET /space-center/part/(id)/cargo-bay.

A CargoBay object is passed and returned as its identifier, a number. A path that acts on an object takes it as (id).

GET /space-center/cargo-bay/(id)/part#

The part object for this cargo bay.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the CargoBay object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (SpaceCenter.Part)

GET /space-center/cargo-bay/(id)/state#

The state of the cargo bay.

Note

This describes where the bay’s doors are, which is not the same as whether the parts inside are sheltered: a bay whose open end has nothing attached to it never shelters anything, however tightly shut it is. Use GET /space-center/part/(id)/shielded for that.

A cargo bay is never "broken", as the game does not track damage for them.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the CargoBay object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (SpaceCenter.DeployableState)

GET /space-center/cargo-bay/(id)/open#

Whether the cargo bay is open.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the CargoBay object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (bool)

PUT /space-center/cargo-bay/(id)/open#

Whether the cargo bay is open.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the CargoBay object.

Request JSON Object:

  • value (bool) – The new value.

Note

Applied when GET /space-center/control-surface/(id)/deployed is true, and clamped to the range given by GET /space-center/control-surface/(id)/min-deploy-angle and GET /space-center/control-surface/(id)/max-deploy-angle. While GET /space-center/control-surface/(id)/deflection-override is enabled, GET /space-center/control-surface/(id)/deflection drives the angle. A value set here takes effect when the override is released.

Note

Applied when GET /space-center/control-surface/(id)/deployed is true, and clamped to the range given by GET /space-center/control-surface/(id)/min-deploy-angle and GET /space-center/control-surface/(id)/max-deploy-angle. While GET /space-center/control-surface/(id)/deflection-override is enabled, GET /space-center/control-surface/(id)/deflection drives the angle. A value set here takes effect when the override is released.

GET /space-center/control-surface/(id)/max-deploy-angle#

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the ControlSurface object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (float)

GET /space-center/control-surface/(id)/deflection-override#

Whether the control surface deflection is being set directly, bypassing the vessel’s normal flight control. When enabled, the surface holds the deflection set by GET /space-center/control-surface/(id)/deflection instead of responding to pitch, yaw and roll control inputs. The prior state is restored when the override is released, when the controlling client disconnects, or when the vessel changes.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the ControlSurface object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (bool)

PUT /space-center/control-surface/(id)/deflection-override#

Whether the control surface deflection is being set directly, bypassing the vessel’s normal flight control. When enabled, the surface holds the deflection set by GET /space-center/control-surface/(id)/deflection instead of responding to pitch, yaw and roll control inputs. The prior state is restored when the override is released, when the controlling client disconnects, or when the vessel changes.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the ControlSurface object.

Request JSON Object:

  • value (bool) – The new value.

GET /space-center/control-surface/(id)/deflection#

The deflection command applied when GET /space-center/control-surface/(id)/deflection-override is enabled, as a value between -1 and 1, mapped onto the surface’s deploy angle range.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the ControlSurface object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (float)

PUT /space-center/control-surface/(id)/deflection#

The deflection command applied when GET /space-center/control-surface/(id)/deflection-override is enabled, as a value between -1 and 1, mapped onto the surface’s deploy angle range.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the ControlSurface object.

Request JSON Object:

Deployable State#

The deployment state shared by antennas, cargo bays, landing legs, radiators, resource harvesters, solar panels and wheels.

DeployableState

The state of a deployable part. GET /space-center/antenna/(id)/state, GET /space-center/cargo-bay/(id)/state, GET /space-center/leg/(id)/state, GET /space-center/radiator/(id)/state, GET /space-center/resource-harvester/(id)/state, GET /space-center/solar-panel/(id)/state, GET /space-center/wheel/(id)/state

Passed and returned as the name of one of its values:

"deployed"

The part is fully deployed. A cargo bay in this state is fully open. Parts that cannot be retracted, such as fixed radiators, solar panels, antennas, landing legs and wheels, are always in this state.

"retracted"

The part is fully retracted. A cargo bay in this state is closed and locked.

"deploying"

The part is being deployed. A cargo bay in this state is opening.

"retracting"

The part is being retracted. A cargo bay in this state is closing.

"broken"

The part is broken. Cargo bays and resource harvesters never report this state, as the game does not track damage for them.

GET /space-center/docking-port/(id)/reference-frame#

The reference frame that is fixed relative to this docking port, and oriented with the port.

  • The origin is at the position of the docking port.

  • The axes rotate with the docking port.

  • The x-axis points out to the right side of the docking port.

  • The y-axis points in the direction the docking port is facing.

  • The z-axis points out of the bottom off the docking port.

Note

This reference frame is not necessarily equivalent to the reference frame for the part, returned by GET /space-center/part/(id)/reference-frame.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the DockingPort object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (SpaceCenter.ReferenceFrame)

DockingPortState

The state of a docking port. See GET /space-center/docking-port/(id)/state.

Passed and returned as the name of one of its values:

"ready"

The docking port is ready to dock to another docking port.

"docked"

The docking port is docked to another docking port, or docked to another part (from the VAB/SPH).

"docking"

The docking port is very close to another docking port, but has not docked. It is using magnetic force to acquire a solid dock.

"undocking"

The docking port has just been undocked from another docking port, and is disabled until it moves away by a sufficient distance (GET /space-center/docking-port/(id)/reengage-distance).

"shielded"

The docking port has a shield, and the shield is closed.

"moving"

The docking ports shield is currently opening/closing.

GET /space-center/engine/(id)/gimbal-response-speed#

The response speed of the gimbal, in \(\mathrm{s^{-1}}\). Throws an exception if the engine is not gimballed.

Note

Each physics tick of length \(\Delta t\), the gimbal moves a fraction \(v \Delta t\) of the way from its deflection to the commanded deflection, where \(v\) is the response speed. The fraction is at most 1, so at high physics warp the gimbal can reach its commanded deflection in one tick. This lag only applies when GET /space-center/engine/(id)/gimbal-response-speed-enabled is true.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Engine object.

  • value (float)

When enabled, the gimbal deflection is set by GET /space-center/engine/(id)/gimbal-actuation instead of the normal control inputs. When enabled, the gimbal deflection is set by GET /space-center/engine/(id)/gimbal-actuation instead of the normal control inputs. The override is automatically released if the controlling client disconnects or the vessel changes. Has no effect if the engine is not gimballed.

GET /space-center/engine/(id)/gimbal-actuation#

The gimbal actuation command applied when GET /space-center/engine/(id)/gimbal-override is enabled, in the pitch, roll and yaw axes. Each component is a normalized control input between -1 and 1. The physical deflection is scaled by GET /space-center/engine/(id)/gimbal-range and GET /space-center/engine/(id)/gimbal-limit. When the gimbal is not being overridden, returns the current actuation.

Note

The gimbal ignores the component for an axis it is disabled for, such as pitch when GET /space-center/engine/(id)/gimbal-pitch-enabled is false.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Engine object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (tuple<double, double, double>)

PUT /space-center/engine/(id)/gimbal-actuation#

The gimbal actuation command applied when GET /space-center/engine/(id)/gimbal-override is enabled, in the pitch, roll and yaw axes. Each component is a normalized control input between -1 and 1. The physical deflection is scaled by GET /space-center/engine/(id)/gimbal-range and GET /space-center/engine/(id)/gimbal-limit. When the gimbal is not being overridden, returns the current actuation.

Note

The gimbal ignores the component for an axis it is disabled for, such as pitch when GET /space-center/engine/(id)/gimbal-pitch-enabled is false.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Engine object.

Request JSON Object:

  • value (tuple<double, double, double>) – The new value.

GET /space-center/engine/(id)/available-torque#

The available torque, in \(\mathrm{N \cdot m}\), that can be produced by this engine, in the positive and negative pitch, roll and yaw axes of the vessel. These axes correspond to the coordinate axes of the GET /space-center/vessel/(id)/reference-frame. Returns zero if the engine is inactive, or not gimballed.

Note

The torque is zero about an axis the gimbal is disabled for, such as pitch when GET /space-center/engine/(id)/gimbal-pitch-enabled is false.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Engine object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (SpaceCenter.AxisRange)

GET /space-center/engine/(id)/can-reverse-thrust#

Whether the engine has a recognized thrust reverser. This is true for stock engines with a thrust reverser (such as the J-33 “Wheesley” and J-90 “Goliath” turbofan engines) and for supported mod engines. It is false for engines whose reverser is not recognized, as KSP provides no standard way to detect one.

Note

Recognizes the thrust reversers of Firespitter and KerbalActuators.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Engine object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (bool)

GET /space-center/engine/(id)/thrust-reversed#

Whether the engine’s thrust reverser is engaged, reversing the direction of thrust. While the reverser is still moving, this reports the state it is moving to, so a read immediately after a set returns the value that was set and setting the same value again has no effect. Throws an exception if the engine does not have a thrust reverser (see GET /space-center/engine/(id)/can-reverse-thrust).

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Engine object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (bool)

PUT /space-center/engine/(id)/thrust-reversed#

Whether the engine’s thrust reverser is engaged, reversing the direction of thrust. While the reverser is still moving, this reports the state it is moving to, so a read immediately after a set returns the value that was set and setting the same value again has no effect. Throws an exception if the engine does not have a thrust reverser (see GET /space-center/engine/(id)/can-reverse-thrust).

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Engine object.

Request JSON Object:

  • value (bool) – The new value.

POST /space-center/engine/(id)/toggle-thrust-reversal#

Toggle the engine’s thrust reverser. Throws an exception if the engine does not have a thrust reverser (see GET /space-center/engine/(id)/can-reverse-thrust).

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Engine object.

GET /space-center/engine/(id)/has-real-fuels#

Whether the engine is managed by RealFuels. The remaining properties in this section are only available when it is.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Engine object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (bool)

GET /space-center/engine/(id)/ignitions#

The number of times the engine can still be ignited, or -1 if it can be ignited an unlimited number of times. Throws an exception if the engine is not managed by RealFuels (see GET /space-center/engine/(id)/has-real-fuels).

Note

Requires RealFuels.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Engine object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (int32)

GET /space-center/engine/(id)/ignition-resources#

The resources the engine consumes each time it ignites, keyed by resource name, with the amount of each that is required. The engine uses up an ignition and fails to light if they are not available. Throws an exception if the engine is not managed by RealFuels (see GET /space-center/engine/(id)/has-real-fuels).

Note

Requires RealFuels.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Engine object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (dictionary<string, double>)

GET /space-center/engine/(id)/has-ullage#

Whether the engine’s propellant is subject to ullage, so that it must be settled before the engine will run reliably. Throws an exception if the engine is not managed by RealFuels (see GET /space-center/engine/(id)/has-real-fuels).

Note

Requires RealFuels.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Engine object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (bool)

GET /space-center/engine/(id)/propellant-stability#

How settled the propellant feeding the engine is, from 0 (fully unsettled) to 1 (fully settled). Acceleration along the engine’s thrust axis settles it, and coasting and rotation unsettle it. Throws an exception if the engine is not managed by RealFuels (see GET /space-center/engine/(id)/has-real-fuels).

Note

Requires RealFuels.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Engine object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (double)

GET /space-center/engine/(id)/propellant-reliability#

The probability that the propellant feeding the engine behaves normally, from 0 to 1. This is GET /space-center/engine/(id)/propellant-stability scaled by the game’s ullage difficulty setting, and is the value RealFuels itself tests against when deciding whether the engine runs. Throws an exception if the engine is not managed by RealFuels (see GET /space-center/engine/(id)/has-real-fuels).

Note

Requires RealFuels.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Engine object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (double)

GET /space-center/engine/(id)/pressure-fed#

Whether the engine is fed by tank pressure rather than by a pump, and so needs to draw from a highly pressurized tank. Throws an exception if the engine is not managed by RealFuels (see GET /space-center/engine/(id)/has-real-fuels).

Note

Requires RealFuels.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Engine object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (bool)

GET /space-center/engine/(id)/has-feed-pressure#

Whether the tanks feeding the engine supply the pressure it needs. Always true for an engine that is not pressure fed. Throws an exception if the engine is not managed by RealFuels (see GET /space-center/engine/(id)/has-real-fuels).

Note

Requires RealFuels.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Engine object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (bool)

ScienceData

Obtained by calling GET /space-center/experiment/(id)/data.

Passed and returned as an object with these fields:

data_amount (float)

Data amount.

science_value (float)

Science value.

transmit_value (float)

Transmit value.

ScienceSubject

Obtained by calling GET /space-center/experiment/(id)/science-subject.

Passed and returned as an object with these fields:

id (string)

The identifier of the subject, e.g. crewReport@KerbinSrfLandedLaunchPad.

title (string)

The title of the subject, as shown in the science archives.

is_complete (bool)

Whether the subject has been fully researched. This is true once the science banked for the subject reaches the science cap. As the banked science (see science) is only updated after transmission/recovery, this reflects fully mining the subject over repeated experiments, not whether a single run has produced data. To check whether a run has produced data, and how valuable it is, use GET /space-center/experiment/(id)/has-data and transmit_value.

science (float)

Amount of science already earned from this subject, not updated until after transmission/recovery.

science_cap (float)

Total science allowable for this subject.

data_scale (float)

Multiply science value by this to determine data amount in mits.

subject_value (float)

Multiplier for specific Celestial Body/Experiment Situation combination.

scientific_value (float)

Diminishing value multiplier for decreasing the science value returned from repeated experiments.

Response JSON Object:

Response JSON Object:

The rise in GET /space-center/leg/(id)/load over one physics tick that breaks the leg, in \(\mathrm{kN}\). Throws an exception if the leg is not breakable.

The multiple of GET /space-center/leg/(id)/impact-tolerance that destroys the leg, in place of breaking it. Throws an exception if the leg is not breakable.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Leg object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (float)

GET /space-center/parachute/(id)/safe-state#

Whether it is currently safe to deploy the parachute, given the vessel’s flight conditions. Computed by KSP from the current airspeed, pressure and temperature. Only applicable to stock parachutes. Note that KSP reports "unsafe" for the first second after the vessel unpacks, before its thermal data is valid.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Parachute object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (SpaceCenter.ParachuteSafeState)

ParachuteState

The state of a parachute. See GET /space-center/parachute/(id)/state.

Passed and returned as the name of one of its values:

"stowed"

The parachute is safely tucked away inside its housing.

"armed"

The parachute is armed for deployment.

"semi_deployed"

The parachute has been deployed and is providing some drag, but is not fully deployed yet. (Stock parachutes only)

"deployed"

The parachute is fully deployed.

"cut"

The parachute has been cut.

ParachuteSafeState

The safety state of deploying a parachute. See GET /space-center/parachute/(id)/safe-state.

Passed and returned as the name of one of its values:

"safe"

The parachute is safe to deploy.

"risky"

Deploying the parachute is risky, and it may break off.

"unsafe"

The parachute is unsafe to deploy, and will break off.

"none"

The safety state is not available, because the vessel is not in an atmosphere or the parachute has already been deployed or cut.

ResourceConverterState

The state of a resource converter. See POST /space-center/resource-converter/(id)/state.

Passed and returned as the name of one of its values:

"running"

Converter is running.

"idle"

Converter is idle.

"missing_resource"

Converter is missing a required resource.

"storage_full"

No available storage for output resource.

"capacity"

At preset resource capacity.

"unknown"

Unknown state. Possible with modified resource converters. In this case, check POST /space-center/resource-converter/(id)/status-info for more information.

Request JSON Object:

  • value (bool) – The new value.

GET /space-center/resource-harvester/(id)/active#

Whether the harvester is actively drilling.

Note

A value set while the harvester is deploying is applied when the deploy completes, so it can be set immediately after setting GET /space-center/resource-harvester/(id)/deployed without waiting for the deploy animation. Setting it has no effect while the harvester is retracted or retracting.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (bool)

Whether the harvester is actively drilling.

Note

A value set while the harvester is deploying is applied when the deploy completes, so it can be set immediately after setting GET /space-center/resource-harvester/(id)/deployed without waiting for the deploy animation. Setting it has no effect while the harvester is retracted or retracting.

GET /space-center/rcs/(id)/input-override#

Whether the RCS control is being set directly, bypassing the vessel’s normal flight controls. When enabled, the rotation and translation demand is set by GET /space-center/rcs/(id)/rotation-override and GET /space-center/rcs/(id)/translation-override instead of the normal control inputs. The override is automatically released if the controlling client disconnects or the vessel changes. Precision mode leaves an overridden block at full thrust.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the RCS object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (bool)

PUT /space-center/rcs/(id)/input-override#

Whether the RCS control is being set directly, bypassing the vessel’s normal flight controls. When enabled, the rotation and translation demand is set by GET /space-center/rcs/(id)/rotation-override and GET /space-center/rcs/(id)/translation-override instead of the normal control inputs. The override is automatically released if the controlling client disconnects or the vessel changes. Precision mode leaves an overridden block at full thrust.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the RCS object.

Request JSON Object:

  • value (bool) – The new value.

GET /space-center/rcs/(id)/rotation-override#

The rotation demand applied when GET /space-center/rcs/(id)/input-override is enabled, in the pitch, roll and yaw axes. Each component is a normalized control input between -1 and 1.

Note

The block ignores the component for an axis it is disabled for, such as pitch when GET /space-center/rcs/(id)/pitch-enabled is false.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the RCS object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (tuple<double, double, double>)

PUT /space-center/rcs/(id)/rotation-override#

The rotation demand applied when GET /space-center/rcs/(id)/input-override is enabled, in the pitch, roll and yaw axes. Each component is a normalized control input between -1 and 1.

Note

The block ignores the component for an axis it is disabled for, such as pitch when GET /space-center/rcs/(id)/pitch-enabled is false.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the RCS object.

Request JSON Object:

  • value (tuple<double, double, double>) – The new value.

GET /space-center/rcs/(id)/translation-override#

The translation demand applied when GET /space-center/rcs/(id)/input-override is enabled, in the right, up and forward axes. Each component is a normalized control input between -1 and 1.

Note

The block ignores the component for an axis it is disabled for, such as right when GET /space-center/rcs/(id)/right-enabled is false.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the RCS object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (tuple<double, double, double>)

PUT /space-center/rcs/(id)/translation-override#

The translation demand applied when GET /space-center/rcs/(id)/input-override is enabled, in the right, up and forward axes. Each component is a normalized control input between -1 and 1.

Note

The block ignores the component for an axis it is disabled for, such as right when GET /space-center/rcs/(id)/right-enabled is false.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the RCS object.

Request JSON Object:

  • value (tuple<double, double, double>) – The new value.

GET /space-center/rcs/(id)/available-torque#

The available torque, in \(\mathrm{N \cdot m}\), that can be produced by this RCS, in the positive and negative pitch, roll and yaw axes of the vessel. These axes correspond to the coordinate axes of the GET /space-center/vessel/(id)/reference-frame. Returns zero if RCS is disable.

Note

Precision mode weakens the block, and the available torque follows it. A block driven by GET /space-center/rcs/(id)/input-override is exempt, so POST /space-center/rcs/(id)/override-wrench can report the larger torque an override reaches.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the RCS object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (SpaceCenter.AxisRange)

GET /space-center/rcs/(id)/available-force#

The available force, in Newtons, that can be produced by this RCS, in the positive and negative x, y and z axes of the vessel. These axes correspond to the coordinate axes of the GET /space-center/vessel/(id)/reference-frame. Returns zero if RCS is disabled.

Note

Precision mode weakens the block, and the available force follows it. A block driven by GET /space-center/rcs/(id)/input-override is exempt, so POST /space-center/rcs/(id)/override-wrench can report the larger force an override reaches.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the RCS object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (SpaceCenter.AxisRange)

GET /space-center/rcs/(id)/force#

The force being applied by the RCS thrusters, in Newtons. The vector is in the vessel’s reference frame (GET /space-center/vessel/(id)/reference-frame). Returns zero if the RCS is inactive.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the RCS object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (tuple<double, double, double>)

GET /space-center/rcs/(id)/torque#

The torque being applied by the RCS thrusters about the vessel’s center of mass, in \(\mathrm{N \cdot m}\). The vector is in the vessel’s reference frame (GET /space-center/vessel/(id)/reference-frame). Returns zero if the RCS is inactive.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the RCS object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (tuple<double, double, double>)

POST /space-center/rcs/(id)/override-wrench#

The force and torque the given demands would produce, in Newtons and \(\mathrm{N \cdot m}\).

Note

The demands do not have to be applied. The prediction leaves out full thrust, which GET /space-center/rcs/(id)/force and GET /space-center/rcs/(id)/torque include.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the RCS object.

Request JSON Object:

  • rotation (tuple<double, double, double>) – A rotation demand, as set by GET /space-center/rcs/(id)/rotation-override.

  • translation (tuple<double, double, double>) – A translation demand, as set by GET /space-center/rcs/(id)/translation-override.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (SpaceCenter.Wrench) – The force, and the torque about the vessel’s center of mass, in the vessel’s reference frame (GET /space-center/vessel/(id)/reference-frame), or zero if the RCS is inactive.

GET /space-center/rcs/(id)/available-thrust#

The amount of thrust, in Newtons, that would be produced by the thruster when activated. Returns zero if the thruster does not have any fuel. Takes the thrusters current GET /space-center/rcs/(id)/thrust-limit and atmospheric conditions into account.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the RCS object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (float)

GET /space-center/rcs/(id)/max-thrust#

The maximum amount of thrust that can be produced by the RCS thrusters when active, in Newtons, with the GET /space-center/rcs/(id)/thrust-limit set to 100%. Takes atmospheric conditions into account.

GET /space-center/sensor/(id)/value#

Note

This is the same readout string shown in the part’s right-click menu in-game, and is intended for display rather than for parsing. Both its units and the way it formats numbers follow the language the game is running in, so it is not stable across locales. For programmatic access to the underlying quantities, use GET /space-center/part/(id)/temperature (temperature sensors), GET /space-center/flight/(id)/g-force (accelerometers) or GET /space-center/flight/(id)/static-pressure (barometers).

Thruster#

Thruster

The component of an Engine or RCS part that generates thrust. Can obtained by calling GET /space-center/engine/(id)/thrusters or GET /space-center/rcs/(id)/thrusters.

Note

Engines can consist of multiple thrusters. For example, the S3 KS-25x4 “Mammoth” has four rocket nozzels, and so consists of four thrusters.

A Thruster object is passed and returned as its identifier, a number. A path that acts on an object takes it as (id).
