Response JSON Object:

  • value (float)

POST /space-center/thruster/(id)/thrust-position#

The position at which the thruster generates thrust, in the given reference frame. For gimballed engines, this takes into account the current rotation of the gimbal.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Thruster object.

Request JSON Object:

  • reference_frame (SpaceCenter.ReferenceFrame) – The reference frame that the returned position vector is in.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (tuple<double, double, double>) – The position as a vector.

POST /space-center/thruster/(id)/thrust-direction#

The direction of the force generated by the thruster, in the given reference frame. This is opposite to the direction in which the thruster expels propellant. For gimballed engines, this takes into account the current rotation of the gimbal.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Thruster object.

Request JSON Object:

  • reference_frame (SpaceCenter.ReferenceFrame) – The reference frame that the returned direction is in.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (tuple<double, double, double>) – The direction as a unit vector.

GET /space-center/thruster/(id)/thrust-reference-frame#

A reference frame that is fixed relative to the thruster and orientated with its thrust direction (POST /space-center/thruster/(id)/thrust-direction). For gimballed engines, this takes into account the current rotation of the gimbal.

  • The origin is at the position of thrust for this thruster (POST /space-center/thruster/(id)/thrust-position).

  • The axes rotate with the thrust direction. This is the direction in which the thruster expels propellant, including any gimballing.

  • The y-axis points along the thrust direction.

  • The x-axis and z-axis are perpendicular to the thrust direction.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Thruster object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (SpaceCenter.ReferenceFrame)

GET /space-center/thruster/(id)/gimballed#

Whether the thruster is gimballed.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Thruster object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (bool)

POST /space-center/thruster/(id)/gimbal-position#

Position around which the gimbal pivots.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Thruster object.

Request JSON Object:

  • reference_frame (SpaceCenter.ReferenceFrame) – The reference frame that the returned position vector is in.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (tuple<double, double, double>) – The position as a vector.

GET /space-center/thruster/(id)/gimbal-angle#

The current gimbal angle in the pitch, roll and yaw axes, in degrees.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Thruster object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (tuple<double, double, double>)

POST /space-center/thruster/(id)/initial-thrust-position#

The position at which the thruster generates thrust, when the engine is in its initial position (no gimballing), in the given reference frame.

Note

This position can move when the gimbal rotates. This is because the thrust position and gimbal position are not necessarily the same.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Thruster object.

Request JSON Object:

  • reference_frame (SpaceCenter.ReferenceFrame) – The reference frame that the returned position vector is in.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (tuple<double, double, double>) – The position as a vector.

POST /space-center/thruster/(id)/initial-thrust-direction#

The direction of the force generated by the thruster, when the engine is in its initial position (no gimballing), in the given reference frame. This is opposite to the direction in which the thruster expels propellant.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Thruster object.

Request JSON Object:

  • reference_frame (SpaceCenter.ReferenceFrame) – The reference frame that the returned direction is in.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (tuple<double, double, double>) – The direction as a unit vector.

Wheel#

Wheel

A wheel. Includes landing gear and rover wheels. Obtained by calling GET /space-center/part/(id)/wheel. Can be used to control the motors, steering and deployment of wheels, among other things.

A Wheel object is passed and returned as its identifier, a number. A path that acts on an object takes it as (id).

GET /space-center/wheel/(id)/suspension-spring#

The spring constant of the suspension, in \(\mathrm{kN/m}\), or null while the wheel is not grounded. Throws an exception if the wheel has no suspension.

Note

The game updates it while the wheel is grounded, from GET /space-center/wheel/(id)/suspension-spring-strength, the vessel’s mass, the wheel’s compression and the local gravity.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Wheel object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (float?)

GET /space-center/wheel/(id)/suspension-damper#

The damping constant of the suspension, in \(\mathrm{kN \cdot s/m}\), or null while the wheel is not grounded. Throws an exception if the wheel has no suspension.

Note

The game updates it while the wheel is grounded, from GET /space-center/wheel/(id)/suspension-damper-strength and GET /space-center/wheel/(id)/suspension-spring.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Wheel object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (float?)

GET /space-center/wheel/(id)/suspension-travel#

The travel of the suspension, in meters.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Wheel object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (float)

GET /space-center/wheel/(id)/load#

The force pressing the wheel into the ground, in \(\mathrm{kN}\).

Note

The game raises the load of a grounded wheel to at least 0.5 kN, or 10 kN for a wheel with the old friction model. GET /space-center/wheel/(id)/impact-tolerance applies to the rise in this value.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Wheel object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (float)

POST /space-center/wheel/(id)/contact-position#

The position of the bottom of the wheel, in the given reference frame. While the wheel is grounded, this is where it touches the ground.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Wheel object.

Request JSON Object:

  • reference_frame (SpaceCenter.ReferenceFrame) – The reference frame that the returned position vector is in.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (tuple<double, double, double>) – The position as a vector.

GET /space-center/wheel/(id)/impact-tolerance#

The rise in GET /space-center/wheel/(id)/load over one physics tick that breaks the wheel, in \(\mathrm{kN}\). Throws an exception if the wheel is not breakable.

Note

The game scales the rise by the local gravity divided by standard gravity before comparing it with this tolerance.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Wheel object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (float)

GET /space-center/wheel/(id)/explode-multiplier#

The multiple of GET /space-center/wheel/(id)/impact-tolerance that destroys the wheel, in place of breaking it. Throws an exception if the wheel is not breakable.

Parameters:

  • id – The identifier of the Wheel object.

Response JSON Object:

  • value (float)

Current stress on the wheel as a percentage of its stress tolerance.

MotorState

The state of the motor on a powered wheel. See GET /space-center/wheel/(id)/motor-state.

Passed and returned as the name of one of its values:

"idle"

The motor is idle.

"running"

The motor is running.

"disabled"

The motor is disabled.

"inoperable"

The motor is inoperable.

"not_enough_resources"

The motor does not have enough resources to run.
